Comment at src/sqllens/rule_sets.py:637-638 sits on IsNotNullRule code that emits NOT(Paren(IS NULL)). MySQL 8.0 operator-precedence docs: with HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE, NOT binds like ! (above IS), so `NOT deleted_at IS NULL` parses as `(NOT deleted_at) IS NULL`. Without the mode, NOT sits below IS. The comment is accurate, and the parentheses make the generated SQL independent of the mode. I did not run MySQL; this rests on the documented precedence rules. Absolute-claim input traced: `NOT deleted_at IS NULL` under HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE.

Doc docs/external/rule-sets.md:197 says a query reaching a renamed or dropped name fails with the database's own error, naming table and column. That holds for a dropped or renamed column: RefusalRedactingRunner.run_sql (src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py:996-1016) catches only RuleSetRefusal, UnsafeSqlError and RlsError, so a pymysql error passes through. It does not hold for a dropped or renamed table. RuleSetGuardRunner always calls the inner runner with require_base_tables=True (rule_sets.py:894-896). The MySQL runner then calls verify_base_tables (agent/integrations/mysql/sql_runner.py:156-157) BEFORE executing the SQL. _verify_relations (safety/relations.py:171-188) looks the table up in information_schema.TABLES. For a missing table kind is None, so it raises RlsError 'row-level security could not verify a base table; query blocked'. RefusalRedactingRunner converts this to REDACTED_RELATION, 'refusing to execute query: the query's relations could not be verified' (rule_sets.py:953-954, 1005-1016). The query never reaches the database, so the client sees a redacted refusal rather than the database's own error. Counterexample: rule-set table renamed or dropped while the server runs. The claim as worded (renamed or dropped name, absolute) is therefore wrong for tables, and the 'error text can name the table' part is also false there. Only column drift matches.

criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text}; criterion 7 matches this item, so it was graded with the criteria file. Implementation: src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py apply_rule_set (798-833) builds a _Scoping with a prefix chosen by _choose_prefix (365-376). That prefix avoids every identifier in the statement and every table name in the set or its rules, ignoring case. When rules is non-empty (always true under a set with a referenced_by link or an inherit/parent_rule rule, since those are row rules), it calls _rename_ctes (379-402) before _analyze and _rewrite. _rename_ctes renames every CTE found by tree.find_all(exp.CTE) to sl<n>_c<k>. It repoints each resolved reference to the new name, keeping the old name as the alias so qualifiers still resolve. The guard-built filter reads of the link table or parent_table are added afterwards, so they cannot be captured by a model CTE. Case variants: a reference that matches the CTE's exact letters is renamed along with it.
